key_insight: The paper shows that partisan LLM agents can be made both ideologically steadfast and factually grounded by combining SFT, DPO, and per-party RAG, enabling interpretable coalition negotiation simulations.
engineering_relevance: It provides a reproducible multi-agent architecture for computational political science, with lineage tracing and agreement auditing that can support transparent scenario testing and policy analysis.
method: Fine-tune party-specific agents with SFT and DPO to induce strong partisan personas.
Attach a per-party RAG pipeline so each agent responds using only its official manifesto.
Use a hub-and-spoke negotiation with a formateur, then trace each agreement clause via MILT and score influence with CIS.
evidence_signal: Across three independent simulations on the 2019 Flemish election, the framework produced a stable ranking (N-VA ahead of CD&V and Open Vld) and manifesto-anchored clauses aligned better with the real coalition agreement than hallucinated content.
watch_item: The approach depends on high-quality manifesto retrieval and carefully calibrated persona tuning; weak grounding or over-aggressive alignment could distort negotiations or provenance tracing.
paper_title: Digital Pantheon: Simulating and Auditing Coalition Formation with LLM Agents
